correction: The campaign did not fail on the first launch: records 001-004 (complete ABBA block 1) are persisted; the interrupt happened in launch 005.
acceptance_semantics: A launch is accepted only when validate_launch passes and write_atomic persists records/NNN.json (tmp file then replace). FAILED/INTERRUPTED/ORPHAN markers and *.tryK.* files are never accepted. load_accepted() re-validates 001-004 against the frozen admission rule and the frozen schedule: all four pass.

launch_005.graceful_wait_exceeded_180s: inferred (not directly observed): the reported traceback is in proc.wait(timeout=60), which graceful_stop reaches only after its 180 s graceful wait expired and proc.terminate() was issued
launch_005.terminate_wait_60s_elapsed: unknown; KeyboardInterrupt arrived inside that wait, so TimeoutExpired was never raised
launch_005.process_alive_afterwards: not determinable from persisted files; check tasklist before resuming

shutdown_latency_release_to_cleaning_up_.note: Ctrl-C is sent immediately after the HTTP response (urlopen returns at ~release). Latency to the server's 'cleaning up' line is therefore the shutdown reaction time. Source: server uptime stamps in each stderr log.

findings: Graceful shutdown works: 001-004 and the four conformance launches all exited gracefully and emitted exactly one policy_timing record.
Reaction latency is heavy-tailed (4.8, 43.9, 79.7, 151.6 s in 001-004; 14.6-39.5 s in conformance), far above the ~5 s of an idle server. 003 used 84% of the 180 s cap; 005 exceeded it.

The stall is BEFORE the 'cleaning up' log line, i.e. in console-signal delivery, the handler, or the main-loop wake-up; not in destructors or policy_timing emission. In the pinned server source the handler path (mcp_mgr.shutdown + queue terminate) contains no waits.

Root cause of the latency is NOT determined from the persisted evidence (candidates: Windows console Ctrl-event delivery to a non-group-leader child, host I/O or memory pressure). No hypothesis is asserted.

Real tooling defects found: (1) a resume would reuse try1 and overwrite the 005 try1 logs; (2) KeyboardInterrupt left no incident state and could leave llama-server running; (3) the 180 s graceful cap is inside the observed latency tail, so it would discard valid inferences (only policy_timing is missing) and make a second failure of some slot likely over 80 launches.
not_a_defect: A manual interrupt of a slow shutdown is not by itself a reason to change code; the changes above are justified by the three defects, not by the interrupt.
inference_values_not_analysed: per-launch timing values in the accepted records were not analysed or used in this incident review; analysis stays deferred to the frozen estimator after 80 accepted launches
